items.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024
items.q: Because Ignacio Berroa, the drummer, actually left there on the Mariel boatlift

ctx.x: Because Ignacio Berroa, the drummer, actually left there on the Mariel boatlift because he felt like he couldn’t stay there and play because the government frowned upon — well he said first The Beatles, they frowned upon The Beatles, but also any jazz type music that seemed like too — you know we call it democratic or based on meritocracy or whatever. But he felt I have to get out of here.

Yup, that’s very true. Paquito too and you know so many of the musicians, yeah, it’s very true. There’s no doubting that’s a fact. And you know some people were totally blackballed, you know like blockaded from doing — the government just had the power to just say no, you’re not going to play. And that actually went on for quite a few years even after, you know a lot of those great musicians left for the U.S., you know people, I know a lot of musicians that somehow were able to hear jazz through Voice of America…
